sections.h2: Where is Virginia Beach and how is the city laid out?
sections.html:
Virginia Beach sits on the Atlantic Ocean at the mouth of the Chesapeake Bay in the southeastern corner of Virginia. It is an independent city, so the same government that runs schools and police also bills property tax, and there is no separate county in the picture.

The city covers 497.5 square miles in total, but only 244.72 of those are land. The rest is water, which makes Virginia Beach the largest city in the state by total area. Average elevation is about 12 feet above sea level, and a large part of the city drains to the Chesapeake Bay through the Lynnhaven River and its tributaries. Norfolk is 19 miles to the west.

A line on the map called the Green Line separates the developed northern part of the city from the rural south. Land north of it is close to built out, which is why many sales here involve older houses in established subdivisions rather than new construction.

sections.h2: How did Virginia Beach become one city?
sections.html:
The resort town was incorporated in 1906, became a city in 1952, and merged with neighboring Princess Anne County in 1963 after voters in both places approved a referendum. Princess Anne County had existed since 1691, so the merger folded more than 250 years of rural county history into one jurisdiction.

The 1883 arrival of rail service to the coast started the resort. The completion of Virginia Beach Boulevard in 1922 opened the route for cars, and The Cavalier Hotel opened in 1927. After the merger the new city was divided into seven boroughs: Bayside, Blackwater, Kempsville, Lynnhaven, Princess Anne, Pungo, and Virginia Beach.

The assessor updates ownership records from deeds, wills, and plats recorded with the Clerk of the Circuit Court.

sections.h2: What do the Assessor and the Treasurer each do in Virginia Beach?
sections.html:
The Real Estate Assessor sets the value of the property, and the City Treasurer sends the bill and collects the money. A third office, the Commissioner of the Revenue, now handles the real estate exemption and freeze programs, according to the Treasurer's page.

Taxes are assessed for the city's fiscal year of July 1 through June 30 and are paid in arrears. If your mortgage company holds an escrow account, the bill goes to the lender. People without escrow receive the bill directly from the Treasurer, and a paid-off mortgage or a change of lender is something you should report so the bill reaches the right place.

  • Assessor questions and appeals: call 757-385-4601 and ask for an appraiser.
  • Board of Equalization: 757-385-6296 or BOE@vbgov.com.
  • Bankruptcy notation on a tax account: email VBBK4you@vbgov.com with the case number.
  • Exemption and freeze programs: ask the Commissioner of the Revenue.

The Treasurer's real estate page also links to a tax search and an open data portal for delinquent real estate.

sections.h2: When are Virginia Beach property taxes due and what if they are late?
sections.html:
Real estate tax is due in two installments, December 5 and June 5, and a due date that lands on a weekend or city holiday moves to the next business day. Partial and advance payments are accepted if you cannot pay a bill in full.

Payments received or postmarked after the grace period carry a penalty of 10% of the total tax or $10, whichever is greater, but never more than the bill plus interest. Interest runs at 9.6% per year. A pending reduction does not excuse the penalty.

Any payment the Treasurer receives is credited first to the most delinquent account, which follows Virginia Code 58.1-3913. If a refund is due after a reduction, the city first checks for other delinquent charges, and the refund takes about four weeks.

  • Late fee: 10% of the tax or $10, whichever is more.
  • Interest: 9.6% per year.
  • Refund timing: about four weeks.
  • Weekend or holiday due date: next business day.

sections.h2: What happens when Virginia Beach taxes stay unpaid for years?
sections.html:
The city can advertise the property and eventually sue to collect. Once taxes are delinquent by three years plus the current tax year, the Treasurer may publish a list of properties with the record owner's name, in a newspaper or online, and charges a $25 advertising fee.

If the taxes are still unpaid on June 30 of the current fiscal year, the account can go to a law firm, and attorney fees are added. A lien may be recorded with the Virginia Beach Circuit Court clerk, after which the city may collect by any legal means, including offering the property for sale.

sections.h2: How does a sale work when real estate tax is still owed on the house?
sections.html:
The unpaid tax is paid out of the sale proceeds at closing, because Virginia law gives the tax lien priority over every other lien or encumbrance on the real estate. Under Code 58.1-3340, that lien stays in place until the taxing authority actually receives payment, and the purchaser or trustee at a sale must see that the proceeds are applied to taxes and levies on the property.

The statute defines taxes and levies to include the penalties and interest. It also says the seller's liability for tax is prorated by contract, which is why the purchase agreement and the settlement statement matter. For the Virginia Beach fiscal year, the Treasurer states that proration is calculated daily from the full annual amount, and that the installment dates do not set separate tax periods.

The treasurer or other proper officer causes the lien to be released once it is paid.

The state also taxes the deed itself. Code 58.1-802 imposes a grantor tax of 50 cents for each $500 of consideration, paid by the seller unless the parties agree that the buyer pays some of it. The clerk must certify payment before a deed is admitted to record.

sections.h2: How do I challenge a Virginia Beach assessment?
sections.html:
Start with a phone call to the Assessor's office, then use the written steps if the answer does not satisfy you. The office says many concerns are settled without additional time and cost, and it recommends the call before any formal appeal.

  • Reassessment notices are mailed by March 1 of each year.
  • Request for Reappraisal: an informal review, accepted March through April 30 of each tax year.
  • Board of Equalization: appeals may be filed from March through June 30 of each tax year.
  • Only the owner or a duly authorized agent may discuss the valuation, and an agent needs an original signed letter of authorization or a notarized power of attorney.

The Board of Equalization has six members appointed by the Circuit Court, and each member must own an interest in real property. Its page refers to hearing appeals for the July 1, 2026 values.

sections.h2: What should a Virginia Beach seller know about flooding and weather?
sections.html:
Water is the main physical risk to a house here. The climate is humid subtropical, with average annual precipitation between 47 inches at the airport and more than 50 inches at Back Bay, and August is the wettest month at over 5.5 inches on average.

Hurricane Matthew's heavy rainfall flooded more than 2,000 homes and left some neighborhoods under standing water for days. After that storm, the city turned down several proposals to build in floodplains. Hurricane Isabel in 2003 is named as the exception to the city's usual position south of major storm tracks, and an EF-3 tornado struck the Great Neck neighborhood on April 30, 2023, with no injuries reported.

Buyers of older houses in low areas tend to ask about past water and drainage.

sections.h2: Which parts of the city and which employers shape the housing market?
sections.html:
Real estate, defense, and tourism are the three sectors that Wikipedia names as major for the Virginia Beach economy. Naval Air Station Oceana, a major Navy fighter jet base, sits inside the city, and homes near it live with the operating constraints that housing growth has placed on the base.

Other institutions based in the city include Regent University, the Christian Broadcasting Network, the U.S. headquarters of Stihl, and the Association for Research and Enlightenment. The Town Center opened in 2003 and the Convention Center in 2005, both built with city help that included tax increment financing districts.

Named communities include Alanton, Cape Henry, Great Neck Point, Green Run, Kempsville, Lynnhaven, Pungo, and Sandbridge. Each has its own mix of ages and conditions.

faqs.q: How much is the Virginia Beach real estate tax bill due in December?
faqs.a: The amount depends on your assessment and the current city rate, so look up your own bill on the City Treasurer's website. The bill is due December 5, with the second installment due June 5.

faqs.q: What is the penalty for paying Virginia Beach real estate tax late?
faqs.a: The penalty is 10% of the total tax or $10, whichever is greater, up to the amount of the bill plus interest, and interest runs at 9.6% per year. A pending reduction does not excuse the penalty, according to the Treasurer.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Virginia Beach house if the property tax is delinquent?
faqs.a: Yes. The unpaid tax, penalty, and interest are paid from the sale proceeds at closing because the tax lien comes ahead of other liens under Code 58.1-3340. Request a payoff figure from the Treasurer before you close.

faqs.q: When can I appeal my Virginia Beach assessment?
faqs.a: You can request a reappraisal from the Assessor from March through April 30, and file with the Board of Equalization from March through June 30 of each tax year. The office suggests calling an appraiser at 757-385-4601 first.

faqs.q: Does the Virginia Beach Treasurer or the Assessor decide my value?
faqs.a: The Real Estate Assessor decides the assessment. The City Treasurer only bills and collects the tax, so assessment questions go to the Assessor and payment questions go to the Treasurer.

faqs.q: Who pays the Virginia grantor tax when a house sells?
faqs.a: By statute the seller, or whoever signs for the seller, pays the 50 cents per $500 grantor tax, although the buyer and seller may agree that the buyer covers some or all of it.
